addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- claude-security:claude-security: The dedicated Claude Security orchestrator. Hand it an unattended job — "fully scan this repository and patch what you find; I understand it will use a lot of tokens" — and it runs the whole thing itself: capturing the revision, driving the multi-agent scan through the claude-security:scan workflow, assembling the verified report, and turning survivors into targeted patch files you apply when you choose, each verified by a panel of agents before it is written. Best as the main agent of a session. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion, Workflow, Workflow(claude-security:scan), TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Agent(claude-security:scan-inventory, claude-security:scan-researcher, claude-security:scan-verifier, claude-security:patch-generator, claude-security:patch-verifier, claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:explore: Read-only code explorer that the plugin's other agents dispatch to map a codebase — locate files, trace how a flow is wired, find every caller of a symbol, answer "where does X happen". (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- claude-security:patch-generator: Implements the fix for one finding inside a scratch workspace clone, staged for review and delivery as a patch file; dispatched by the fix job, not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:patch-verifier: The single verifier per fix round — reviews the workspace's staged diff against the finding, runs the tests, and states the three confidence claims a patch file must earn; dispatched by the fix job, not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:scan-inventory: Restricted read-only repository cartographer dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow to partition the tree into components and account for every top-level directory; not for direct invocation or vulnerability research. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- claude-security:scan-researcher: Restricted read-only vulnerability researcher dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow; not for direct invocation or general exploration. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:scan-verifier: Restricted read-only verifier dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow to vote on one candidate finding; not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- code-review: Expert Go, GCP, and OpenTofu code reviewer. Invoke against the branch diff plus all staged, unstaged, and untracked files before every commit, and again before a pull request only when the reviewed state changed. Issues an approval or actionable revision request; does not fix code. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- ui-review: Expert reviewer for website design, usability, responsiveness, and accessibility. Invoke after an implementation pass when a change can affect rendered UI — templates, static assets, styling, or a client app. Reports findings; does not fix them. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_navigate, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_snapshot, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_take_screenshot, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_click, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_fill_form, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_press_key, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_resize, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_console_messages, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_network_requests, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_wait_for, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_close)
- verifier: Runs focused integration or journey checks during TDD, or the complete verification gate after implementation settles. Reports findings; does not fix them. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

content.content:
1	# Agent Workflow Guidelines
2	
3	This document defines the standard workflow required for all AI coding agents
4	working on this codebase, and it is the single source of truth for that
5	workflow. Every agent reads this file. Tool-specific entrypoints such as
6	`CLAUDE.md` only point here — never add rules, commands, or project facts to
7	them, because agents that read a different entrypoint will not see them. Add it
8	here instead. Registered subagent definitions may describe their role and
9	reporting format, but they must defer project facts, gate applicability, and
10	verification commands to this file.
11	
12	## The project
13	
14	Event-driven Go microservices for reporting and matching lost pets, running on
15	GCP (Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Firestore, GCS) and locally via Docker Compose plus
16	Ollama `gemma4:e2b`.
17	
18	The repository has five services. Four expose JSON HTTP endpoints or run as
19	Pub/Sub workers; `web-frontend` serves rendered HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and JSON
20	API endpoints. The Playwright suite contains both API-level request journeys
21	and browser-driven page coverage.
22	
23	| Path | Contents |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| `cmd/` | Service entrypoints: `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, `pet-matcher`, `notification-service`, `web-frontend` |
26	| `pkg/` | Shared packages: `domain`, `store`, `pubsub`, `blob`, `ollama`, `scoring` |
27	| `e2e/` | Self-contained Go event-cascade tests using in-memory and test servers |
28	| `tests/playwright/` | API and browser journeys using three local HTTP services |
29	| `infra/opentofu/` | GCP infrastructure modules |
30	| `deploy/cloudrun/` | Cloud Run manifests |
31	| `docs/` | `DEVELOPMENT.md`, `MIGRATION_PLAN.md` |
32	
33	## Code Review Rules
34	
35	These rules guide local reviewers. Keep deterministic formatting, lint, build,
36	and test checks in the verifier and CI.
37	
38	- Pub/Sub handlers must remain idempotent under redelivery. Flag writes,
39	  notifications, or state transitions that can be duplicated when the same
40	  event is delivered more than once; use a stable event or deduplication key,
41	  or make the operation inherently idempotent.
42	- Event schema changes must remain backward compatible with in-flight
43	  messages. Prefer additive fields with tolerant readers; otherwise introduce
44	  an explicit version and preserve a decoder or migration path for the prior
45	  schema.
46	- Reporter contact details and state-changing actions must not cross an
47	  unauthenticated or unauthorized boundary. Apply this rule to new or changed
48	  boundaries: return redacted public DTOs and require authentication plus
49	  ownership or equivalent authorization before exposing contact data or
50	  mutating pet and match state. Existing pre-authentication demo behavior is
51	  roadmap debt, not precedent for expanding the exposed boundary.
52	
53	## Ground rules
54	
55	These apply at every step, not just at the gate where they are mentioned.
56	
57	- **Never commit directly to `main`.** Never force-push, never amend or rebase
58	  a commit that has already been pushed, and never discard user work with
59	  `git checkout --`, `git restore`, `git clean`, or `git reset --hard`.
60	- **Preserve unrelated work.** Staged, unstaged, and untracked files that you
61	  did not create belong to the user. Leave them alone.
62	- **Never commit secrets.** No service-account JSON, `*.tfstate`, `.env` files,
63	  API keys, or real GCP project identifiers. If you need a credential to
64	  proceed, stop and ask.
65	- **Stop and ask the user** rather than pushing through when: a gate fails
66	  twice for the same reason; the task requires a credential, a paid resource,
67	  or a destructive operation; the change would alter published API contracts,
68	  infrastructure state, or CI enforcement; or the request is ambiguous enough
69	  that two readings produce materially different work.
70	
71	## Workflow
72	
73	1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git
74	   state, and all applicable instruction files before making changes.
75	
76	2. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or
77	   feature, define the smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested,
78	   shipped, and merged independently. Prefer one coherent user-visible or
79	   operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the next issue is too
80	   large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only
81	   the current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review,
82	   reliable verification, and quick rollback.
83	
84	3. **Create a branch for that slice.** Branch from the latest `main` using
85	   `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`, where `<type>` is one of `feat`, `fix`,
86	   `refactor`, `chore`, `test`, or `docs` — matching the Conventional Commit
87	   type the work will land under. Example: `feat/foundpet-image-upload`.
88	
89	4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
90	   - Add or update a focused test before implementation.
91	   - Run it and confirm it fails for the expected reason.
92	   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
93	   - Run focused tests while iterating.
94	   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.
95	   - Follow [Test execution ownership](#test-execution-ownership) so the main
96	     agent retains only focused Go test output and the verifier owns noisy or
97	     repository-wide execution.
98	
99	5. **Inspect the complete diff and track out-of-scope discoveries.** Review the
100	   branch diff plus all staged, unstaged, and untracked files. Remove
101	   accidental or unrelated changes while preserving work that belongs to the
102	   user. Whenever you discover bugs, technical debt, missing features, or
103	   refactoring opportunities not aligned with the current slice, file them with
104	   `gh issue create` rather than expanding scope. Title them as Conventional
105	   Commits, label them `agent-found`, and reference the branch that surfaced
106	   them. Filing these issues is pre-authorized; you do not need to ask first.
107	
108	6. **Run `ui-review` when the change can affect rendered UI.** Invoke the
109	   `ui-review` sub-agent after an implementation pass. See
110	   [Applicability](#applicability) for when this gate is live. When it applies,
111	   exercise the changed journey in the rendered application at representative
112	   phone, tablet, and desktop viewports; inspect interaction, loading, empty,
113	   error, focus, keyboard, contrast, and responsive states; and capture
114	   screenshots or equivalent visual evidence. Address every actionable finding
115	   before running the `verifier`. When the change has no UI impact, record one
116	   line stating that and move on — do not fabricate a review.
117	
118	7. **Run `verifier` before code review.** Invoke the `verifier` sub-agent to run
119	   the builds, static checks, tests, and journey coverage appropriate for the
120	   change. The verifier must report failures, flakes, missing coverage, and
121	   environment issues, and must state explicitly which suites it could not run
122	   and why (for example, the local HTTP services required by Playwright could
123	   not be started). Fix or explicitly resolve every actionable finding before
124	   starting code review. If a verifier finding requires a code change, rerun
125	   the verifier after addressing it. A focused-support verifier run during TDD
126	   does not satisfy this gate; invoke the verifier fresh against the settled
127	   worktree for the complete applicable battery.
128	
129	8. **Run the local `code-review` before every commit.** Invoke the
130	    `code-review` sub-agent against the current branch diff and every staged,
131	    unstaged, and untracked file. Address every actionable finding before
132	    committing. If review findings cause changes, rerun the affected tests and
133	    the `verifier`, then obtain a fresh `code-review` approval for the changed
134	    state.
135	
136	9. **Commit after approval.** Commit only after verification and code review are
137	   complete. Use Conventional Commits:
138	
139	   ```text
140	   <type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>
141	   ```
142	
143	   Keep the subject at 72 characters or fewer, describe why in the body when
144	   useful, and do not combine unrelated work.
145	
146	10. **Create pull requests from the reviewed state.**
147	    - Confirm that local verification remains valid.
148	    - Rerun `code-review` only if the reviewed state changed after the
149	      pre-commit review. A changed state includes code, tests, documentation,
150	      generated files, conflict resolution, or any other staged, unstaged, or
151	      untracked content. Do not repeat code review when the already-reviewed
152	      diff and worktree remain unchanged.
153	    - Title the pull request as a Conventional Commit. CI enforces this, and
154	      because short-lived branches are squash-merged, the pull request title
155	      becomes the commit subject on `main`.
156	    - Push and open a normal, ready-for-review pull request. Do not open draft
157	      pull requests unless the user explicitly asks for a draft.

159	11. **Merge only clean, passing pull requests.** Merge only after GitHub reports
160	    a clean merge state and every configured check passes. Never bypass a
161	    failing or pending required check. Self-merges are allowed when these
162	    conditions are met. Use squash merge for short-lived development branches to
163	    keep `main` linear, then delete the merged branch.
164	
165	## Gate discipline
166	
167	The `ui-review` → `verifier` → `code-review` sequence can otherwise loop
168	forever. It is bounded by these rules.
169	
170	- **Actionable** means correctness, security, data-loss, accessibility, or
171	  contract defects, plus anything the sub-agent marks as blocking. Style
172	  preferences and speculative refactors are not actionable; note them, or file
173	  them per step 5, and move on.
174	- **Two rounds maximum.** If the same gate reports actionable findings on a
175	  third pass, stop and hand the disagreement to the user with both positions
176	  summarized.
177	- **Rerun only what the change invalidated.** A documentation-only fix after a
178	  review does not require rerunning the full verifier suite; say what you
179	  reran and why.
180	- **Never self-certify a gate.** If a sub-agent is unavailable, say so
181	  explicitly and state what you checked manually instead. Do not report a gate
182	  as passed when it did not run.
183	
184	## Test execution ownership
185	
186	Keep the main agent's context focused on design and implementation. Split test
187	execution by phase and weight:
188	
189	| Phase | Main agent | `verifier` sub-agent |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| Go TDD red/green | Writes the test and runs only the exact focused Go test, scoped by package and `-run` | Not required |
192	| Integration or journey TDD red/green | Writes the focused contract and interprets the concise result | Runs only the named emulator, Docker, or Playwright test in focused-support mode |
193	| Settled implementation gate | Does not duplicate the full battery | Starts fresh and runs every applicable command in [Verification scope](#verification-scope) |
194	
195	The main agent may rerun a tightly related set of named Go tests while
196	refactoring, but it does not run repository-wide tests, race/coverage, lint,
197	Compose rebuilds, emulator batteries, infrastructure validation, or
198	Playwright. A focused Go test already compiles its package; do not add a broad
199	build merely to prove compilation during the TDD loop.
200	
201	All automated Playwright execution belongs to the verifier, including a single
202	spec or test selected for journey TDD. In focused-support mode, the verifier
203	reports the command, the red or green result, and the decisive failure evidence
204	without claiming the formal gate. After the implementation settles, use a
205	fresh verifier invocation for the full applicable suite. Manual viewport and
206	accessibility inspection remains the separate `ui-review` responsibility.
207	
208	## Applicability
209	
210	Not every gate applies to every change. Record the reason when one does not.
211	
212	| Gate | Applies when | Status in this repo |
213	| --- | --- | --- |
214	| `ui-review` | The change affects rendered UI — templates, static assets, styling, or a client app | **Live.** Active for `cmd/web-frontend` templates and CSS. |
215	| `verifier` | Always | Live |
216	| `code-review` | Always | Live |
217	
218	The Playwright suite in `tests/playwright/` contains both API request specs and
219	browser-driven page specs. The verifier owns all automated Playwright coverage;
220	browser specs complement but do not replace the manual, viewport-based
221	`ui-review` gate for rendered UI changes.
222	
223	## Verification scope
224	
225	The `verifier` owns these commands.
226	
227	**Every tool version is pinned to match CI.** Reproduce a CI failure with the
228	pinned version, never `@latest` — a floating linter once produced a green local
229	run and a red CI on the same commit. If you change a version here, change it in
230	`.github/workflows/ci.yml` in the same commit.
231	
232	Go toolchain — `1.26.5`, matching `actions/setup-go` in CI. The Go version is
233	pinned for the same reason the linters are: `go vet`'s analyzer set and stdlib
234	behavior shift between releases, so a newer local toolchain can pass checks that
235	CI rejects. `go.mod` declares `go 1.22` as the **language** version, which is a
236	separate thing and does not pin the toolchain. Check yours before verifying:
237	
238	```bash
239	go version   # must report go1.26.5
240	```
241	
242	Static checks and unit tests — always:
243	
244	```bash
245	go vet ./...
246	go test -race -cover ./...
247	```
248	
249	Go lint — always. `.golangci.yml` uses the **v2** config schema, which a v1
250	binary cannot parse:
251	
252	```bash
253	go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run
254	```
255	
256	Markdown lint — when Markdown changes:
257	
258	```bash
259	npx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.49.1 --config .markdownlint.json \
260	  "AGENTS.md" "CLAUDE.md" "README.md" "docs/**/*.md"
261	```
262	
263	Infrastructure — when `infra/` changes. `tofu fmt` output can differ between
264	versions, so use OpenTofu `1.12.5`:
265	
266	```bash
267	cd infra/opentofu
268	tofu fmt -check -recursive
269	tofu init -backend=false && tofu validate
270	```
271	
272	The always-on `go test -race -cover ./...` command includes `e2e/`, which is
273	self-contained in-process cascade coverage backed by in-memory components and
274	test HTTP servers. It does not require Compose, Ollama, or GCP credentials.
275	
276	Playwright journey coverage — when HTTP service behavior, rendered pages, or
277	contracts change. It needs only the three HTTP services exercised by the suite;
278	if they cannot run, the verifier must report `NOT RUN` with the reason rather
279	than silently skipping:
280	
281	```bash
282	docker compose up --build --detach lostpet-service foundpet-service web-frontend
283	
284	cd tests/playwright
285	npm ci
286	npx playwright install chromium
287	npx playwright test
288	```
289	
290	## CI
291	
292	`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs five jobs on pull requests. The first four are
293	required before merge:
294	
295	- `pr-title` — validates the **PR title** as a Conventional Commit. Because
296	  short-lived branches are squash-merged, the PR title becomes the commit
297	  subject on `main`.
298	- `static-checks` — markdownlint. The file list is hardcoded in the workflow;
299	  renaming or adding a top-level doc requires updating it in the same commit.
300	- `go-checks` — `go vet`, `go test -race -cover`, `golangci-lint`.
301	- `infra-checks` — `tofu fmt -check -recursive` and `tofu validate`.
302	- `e2e-playwright-tests` — builds the three HTTP services used by the Playwright
303	  API and browser journeys, waits for them to become ready, runs the suite, and
304	  uploads its report, traces, and service logs on failure. This job is not a
305	  required check until the repository ruleset is updated separately.
306	
307	The `go-checks` job runs the self-contained `e2e/` package as part of
308	`go test -race -cover ./...`. The Playwright job needs only `lostpet-service`,
309	`foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`, so it deliberately avoids downloading a
310	model. Neither CI nor the documented verifier commands exercise a live Ollama,
311	real Pub/Sub, or deployed GCP cascade; do not claim that coverage unless a task
312	defines and runs an explicit integration command for it. CI results also do not
313	replace the independent verifier report required by step 7.
314	
315	## Branch protection
316	
317	`main` is protected by an active ruleset: pull request required, squash-only
318	merges, no deletion, no force-push, and all four checks green before merge.
319	There are no bypass actors — it applies to repository owners too, which is what
320	makes step 11 enforceable rather than aspirational.
321	
322	Required status checks are **strict**: a branch must also be up to date with
323	`main` before it can merge. If GitHub reports `BLOCKED` while every check is
324	green, the branch is behind — update it from `main`, let CI rerun, and confirm
325	a clean state again. Merging `main` in changes the reviewed state, so step 10's
326	rerun rule applies: a conflict resolution needs a fresh `code-review`, while a
327	clean fast-forward update does not.
328	
329	The required check contexts must match the job `name:` values in `ci.yml`
330	exactly. Renaming a job without updating the ruleset leaves a required check
331	that can never report, which blocks every pull request.
332	
333	## Registered subagents
334	
335	These are defined in `.claude/agents/` and are invocable by name. If you are
336	running under a tool that cannot load them, follow the responsibilities below
337	inline and say that you did so.
338	
339	### `ui-review`
340	
341	- **Role**: Website design, usability, responsiveness, and accessibility
342	  expert.
343	- **Responsibilities**:
344	  - Exercises UI user journeys across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports.
345	  - Inspects interaction, loading, empty, error, focus, keyboard navigation,
346	    contrast, and responsive layout states.
347	  - Captures visual evidence and screenshots.
348	  - Documents UI findings, or states plainly that the change has no UI impact.
349	  - Identifies out-of-scope UI defects and files issues per step 5.
350	
351	### `verifier`
352	
353	- **Role**: Build, static check, test, and journey coverage verifier.
354	- **Responsibilities**:
355	  - Supports TDD by running an explicitly named integration, emulator, Docker,
356	    or Playwright test when requested, returning a concise result without
357	    treating it as the formal gate.
358	  - Executes the commands in [Verification scope](#verification-scope).
359	  - Runs the formal gate fresh against the settled worktree even when it ran

361	  - Reports failures, flakes, missing coverage, and environment configuration
362	    issues, and names every suite it could not run.
363	  - Validates code fixes before code review begins.
364	  - Flags pre-existing test debt or environmental issues outside the current
365	    scope and files issues per step 5.
366	
367	### `code-review`
368	
369	- **Role**: Language, framework, and architectural code review expert.
370	- **Responsibilities**:
371	  - Inspects branch diffs and all staged, unstaged, and untracked files against
372	    best practices, security standards, and performance patterns.
373	  - Verifies Conventional Commit messages, API design consistency, and clean
374	    code principles.
375	  - Issues a formal approval or actionable revision request before commits and
376	    pull requests.
377	  - Identifies unrelated code smells, technical debt, or bugs and files issues
378	    per step 5 rather than coupling them to the pull request.

# Agent Workflow Guidelines

This document defines the standard workflow required for all AI coding agents
working on this codebase, and it is the single source of truth for that
workflow. Every agent reads this file. Tool-specific entrypoints such as
`CLAUDE.md` only point here — never add rules, commands, or project facts to
them, because agents that read a different entrypoint will not see them. Add it
here instead. Registered subagent definitions may describe their role and
reporting format, but they must defer project facts, gate applicability, and
verification commands to this file.

## The project

Event-driven Go microservices for reporting and matching lost pets, running on
GCP (Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Firestore, GCS) and locally via Docker Compose plus
Ollama `gemma4:e2b`.

The repository has five services. Four expose JSON HTTP endpoints or run as
Pub/Sub workers; `web-frontend` serves rendered HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and JSON
API endpoints. The Playwright suite contains both API-level request journeys
and browser-driven page coverage.

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/` | Service entrypoints: `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, `pet-matcher`, `notification-service`, `web-frontend` |
| `pkg/` | Shared packages: `domain`, `store`, `pubsub`, `blob`, `ollama`, `scoring` |
| `e2e/` | Self-contained Go event-cascade tests using in-memory and test servers |
| `tests/playwright/` | API and browser journeys using three local HTTP services |
| `infra/opentofu/` | GCP infrastructure modules |
| `deploy/cloudrun/` | Cloud Run manifests |
| `docs/` | `DEVELOPMENT.md`, `MIGRATION_PLAN.md` |

## Code Review Rules

These rules guide local reviewers. Keep deterministic formatting, lint, build,
and test checks in the verifier and CI.

- Pub/Sub handlers must remain idempotent under redelivery. Flag writes,
  notifications, or state transitions that can be duplicated when the same
  event is delivered more than once; use a stable event or deduplication key,
  or make the operation inherently idempotent.
- Event schema changes must remain backward compatible with in-flight
  messages. Prefer additive fields with tolerant readers; otherwise introduce
  an explicit version and preserve a decoder or migration path for the prior
  schema.
- Reporter contact details and state-changing actions must not cross an
  unauthenticated or unauthorized boundary. Apply this rule to new or changed
  boundaries: return redacted public DTOs and require authentication plus
  ownership or equivalent authorization before exposing contact data or
  mutating pet and match state. Existing pre-authentication demo behavior is
  roadmap debt, not precedent for expanding the exposed boundary.

## Ground rules

These apply at every step, not just at the gate where they are mentioned.

- **Never commit directly to `main`.** Never force-push, never amend or rebase
  a commit that has already been pushed, and never discard user work with
  `git checkout --`, `git restore`, `git clean`, or `git reset --hard`.
- **Preserve unrelated work.** Staged, unstaged, and untracked files that you
  did not create belong to the user. Leave them alone.
- **Never commit secrets.** No service-account JSON, `*.tfstate`, `.env` files,
  API keys, or real GCP project identifiers. If you need a credential to
  proceed, stop and ask.
- **Stop and ask the user** rather than pushing through when: a gate fails
  twice for the same reason; the task requires a credential, a paid resource,
  or a destructive operation; the change would alter published API contracts,
  infrastructure state, or CI enforcement; or the request is ambiguous enough
  that two readings produce materially different work.

## Workflow

1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git
   state, and all applicable instruction files before making changes.

2. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or
   feature, define the smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested,
   shipped, and merged independently. Prefer one coherent user-visible or
   operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the next issue is too
   large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only
   the current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review,
   reliable verification, and quick rollback.

3. **Create a branch for that slice.** Branch from the latest `main` using
   `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`, where `<type>` is one of `feat`, `fix`,
   `refactor`, `chore`, `test`, or `docs` — matching the Conventional Commit
   type the work will land under. Example: `feat/foundpet-image-upload`.

4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
   - Add or update a focused test before implementation.
   - Run it and confirm it fails for the expected reason.
   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
   - Run focused tests while iterating.
   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.
   - Follow [Test execution ownership](#test-execution-ownership) so the main
     agent retains only focused Go test output and the verifier owns noisy or
     repository-wide execution.

5. **Inspect the complete diff and track out-of-scope discoveries.** Review the
   branch diff plus all staged, unstaged, and untracked files. Remove
   accidental or unrelated changes while preserving work that belongs to the
   user. Whenever you discover bugs, technical debt, missing features, or
   refactoring opportunities not aligned with the current slice, file them with
   `gh issue create` rather than expanding scope. Title them as Conventional
   Commits, label them `agent-found`, and reference the branch that surfaced
   them. Filing these issues is pre-authorized; you do not need to ask first.

6. **Run `ui-review` when the change can affect rendered UI.** Invoke the
   `ui-review` sub-agent after an implementation pass. See
   [Applicability](#applicability) for when this gate is live. When it applies,
   exercise the changed journey in the rendered application at representative
   phone, tablet, and desktop viewports; inspect interaction, loading, empty,
   error, focus, keyboard, contrast, and responsive states; and capture
   screenshots or equivalent visual evidence. Address every actionable finding
   before running the `verifier`. When the change has no UI impact, record one
   line stating that and move on — do not fabricate a review.

7. **Run `verifier` before code review.** Invoke the `verifier` sub-agent to run
   the builds, static checks, tests, and journey coverage appropriate for the
   change. The verifier must report failures, flakes, missing coverage, and
   environment issues, and must state explicitly which suites it could not run
   and why (for example, the local HTTP services required by Playwright could
   not be started). Fix or explicitly resolve every actionable finding before
   starting code review. If a verifier finding requires a code change, rerun
   the verifier after addressing it. A focused-support verifier run during TDD
   does not satisfy this gate; invoke the verifier fresh against the settled
   worktree for the complete applicable battery.

8. **Run the local `code-review` before every commit.** Invoke the
    `code-review` sub-agent against the current branch diff and every staged,
    unstaged, and untracked file. Address every actionable finding before
    committing. If review findings cause changes, rerun the affected tests and
    the `verifier`, then obtain a fresh `code-review` approval for the changed
    state.

9. **Commit after approval.** Commit only after verification and code review are
   complete. Use Conventional Commits:

   ```text
   <type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>
   ```

   Keep the subject at 72 characters or fewer, describe why in the body when
   useful, and do not combine unrelated work.

10. **Create pull requests from the reviewed state.**
    - Confirm that local verification remains valid.
    - Rerun `code-review` only if the reviewed state changed after the
      pre-commit review. A changed state includes code, tests, documentation,
      generated files, conflict resolution, or any other staged, unstaged, or
      untracked content. Do not repeat code review when the already-reviewed
      diff and worktree remain unchanged.
    - Title the pull request as a Conventional Commit. CI enforces this, and
      because short-lived branches are squash-merged, the pull request title
      becomes the commit subject on `main`.
    - Push and open a normal, ready-for-review pull request. Do not open draft
      pull requests unless the user explicitly asks for a draft.

11. **Merge only clean, passing pull requests.** Merge only after GitHub reports
    a clean merge state and every configured check passes. Never bypass a
    failing or pending required check. Self-merges are allowed when these
    conditions are met. Use squash merge for short-lived development branches to
    keep `main` linear, then delete the merged branch.

The `ui-review` → `verifier` → `code-review` sequence can otherwise loop
forever. It is bounded by these rules.

- **Actionable** means correctness, security, data-loss, accessibility, or
  contract defects, plus anything the sub-agent marks as blocking. Style

  third pass, stop and hand the disagreement to the user with both positions

- **Rerun only what the change invalidated.** A documentation-only fix after a
  review does not require rerunning the full verifier suite; say what you
  reran and why.

execution by phase and weight:

| Phase | Main agent | `verifier` sub-agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go TDD red/green | Writes the test and runs only the exact focused Go test, scoped by package and `-run` | Not required |
| Integration or journey TDD red/green | Writes the focused contract and interprets the concise result | Runs only the named emulator, Docker, or Playwright test in focused-support mode |
| Settled implementation gate | Does not duplicate the full battery | Starts fresh and runs every applicable command in [Verification scope](#verification-scope) |

fresh verifier invocation for the full applicable suite. Manual viewport and
accessibility inspection remains the separate `ui-review` responsibility.

| Gate | Applies when | Status in this repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui-review` | The change affects rendered UI — templates, static assets, styling, or a client app | **Live.** Active for `cmd/web-frontend` templates and CSS. |
| `verifier` | Always | Live |
| `code-review` | Always | Live |

- **Responsibilities**:

    contrast, and responsive layout states.
  - Captures visual evidence and screenshots.
  - Documents UI findings, or states plainly that the change has no UI impact.
  - Identifies out-of-scope UI defects and files issues per step 5.

### `verifier`

- **Role**: Build, static check, test, and journey coverage verifier.
- **Responsibilities**:
  - Supports TDD by running an explicitly named integration, emulator, Docker,
    or Playwright test when requested, returning a concise result without
    treating it as the formal gate.
  - Executes the commands in [Verification scope](#verification-scope).
  - Runs the formal gate fresh against the settled worktree even when it ran
    focused-support checks earlier in the slice.
  - Reports failures, flakes, missing coverage, and environment configuration
    issues, and names every suite it could not run.
  - Validates code fixes before code review begins.
  - Flags pre-existing test debt or environmental issues outside the current
    scope and files issues per step 5.

### `code-review`

- **Role**: Language, framework, and architectural code review expert.
- **Responsibilities**:
  - Inspects branch diffs and all staged, unstaged, and untracked files against
    best practices, security standards, and performance patterns.
  - Verifies Conventional Commit messages, API design consistency, and clean
    code principles.
  - Issues a formal approval or actionable revision request before commits and
    pull requests.
  - Identifies unrelated code smells, technical debt, or bugs and files issues
    per step 5 rather than coupling them to the pull request.

<class 'dict'> ['confirmed', 'report']
## Verdict

The workflow makes sense, and it is better designed than most documents of its kind. The core loop — thin vertical slice → branch → TDD → `ui-review` → `verifier` → `code-review` → commit → PR → merge — is coherent, and the parts that usually go wrong elsewhere are explicitly handled here: the gate sequence is bounded by a two-round cap and a "never self-certify" rule, test execution is split by phase so the main agent's context stays clean, every gate has a stated applicability with a "record the reason when it does not apply" requirement, tool versions are pinned with a real justification, and branch protection is described accurately down to the strict-checks `BLOCKED` case. The single-source-of-truth discipline is enforced mechanically, not just asserted: `docs/docs_test.go` fails CI when this file drifts from `ci.yml`, and `.claude/agents/*.md` are forbidden from inlining versions or commands. That is unusually rigorous.

The defects are not structural. Every one is a **map-vs-territory** problem: the workflow logic is sound, but a handful of factual statements about the repository have gone stale as the code moved ahead of the document, and two capability gaps mean a live gate can be reached with no documented way to satisfy it. The highest-value fixes are three sentences and one table cell.

## Findings

### 1. The `ui-review` Status cell excludes client-side JavaScript, contradicting its own row and the agent definition

content.text:
Spot-checks confirm the factual findings. Here's the verdict.

## The workflow itself is sound

The core loop — thin slice → branch → TDD → `ui-review` → `verifier` → `code-review` → commit → PR → squash-merge — holds up under a literal read. The things that usually break documents like this are explicitly handled: the gate sequence is bounded (two-round cap + "never self-certify"), test execution is split by phase so the main agent's context stays clean, every gate has stated applicability with a record-the-reason rule, and branch protection is described accurately down to the strict-checks `BLOCKED` case. Single-source-of-truth isn't just asserted — `docs/docs_test.go` fails required CI when AGENTS.md drifts from `ci.yml`.

**Every real defect is map-vs-territory: the code moved ahead of the document.** Nine findings survived adversarial verification (out of a larger candidate set — the verifiers killed several as misreadings).

## Worth fixing

**1. `ui-review` Status cell is stale — line 214.** Says "templates and CSS," but six JS files now exist (`static/js/lost-wizard.js`, `match-dashboard.js`, `push-notifier.js`, `theme.js`, `found-report.js`, `sw.js`), all added after that cell was written. The Applies-when column in the same row already says "client app." An agent changing the match dashboard reads the Status cell, records "no UI impact," and skips the only accessibility gate.

**2. Emulator contracts skip silently — lines 27, 271–274.** `e2e/firestore_process_test.go` and `e2e/pubsub_push_test.go` `t.Skip` unless `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`/`PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST` are set. Nothing in Verification scope or `go-checks` starts an emulator, so the package prints `ok` having run half its tests — and the skipped half covers exactly the redelivery-idempotency rule at lines 38–41. The doc calls `e2e/` "self-contained."

**3. The live `ui-review` gate has no documented bring-up — step 6.** The only app-start command sits under "The `verifier` owns these commands," but step 6 requires ui-review to run *before* the verifier, and lines 196–199 bar the main agent from Compose. `web-frontend` builds standalone on 8082 with no `depends_on`; nothing says so.

**4. `pkg/` row lists 6 packages; 10 exist — line 26.** Missing `outbox`, `delivery`, `runtimeconfig`, `telemetry`. An agent scoping idempotency work won't learn `pkg/outbox` exists. (`docs/` row also misses `ROADMAP.md`.)

**5. The doc never says its own wording is machine-asserted — lines 227–230.** `docs_test.go` matches version pins by literal regex. Rewording ``Go toolchain — `1.26.5` `` to `Go toolchain: 1.26.5` turns a required job red from a prose edit. The audit itself tripped this guard while drafting a fix.

**6. The toolchain check has no else-branch — lines 232–240.** Says `go version` must report `go1.26.5`, then stops. `go.mod`'s `go 1.22` prevents `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` from fetching it; the fix is `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.5`.

**7. Node is unpinned** despite "**Every** tool version is pinned to match CI." CI pins `node-version: 20` in two jobs; local is v26. Latent, but it's the one omission from a bolded absolute.

**8. No issue/PR linkage guidance.** The repo has a firm convention (`Closes #108.` on the final slice, `Part of #108.` on earlier ones) that's nowhere in the doc. Bad path: `Closes` on slice 1 of an ordered split auto-closes the epic on squash merge.

**9. Line 326 exempts an unreachable case.** "A clean fast-forward update does not [need re-review]" — a PR branch with its own commits can't fast-forward, and rebase is barred by line 57. Should read "a conflict-free update."

One non-AGENTS.md item: `.claude/agents/ui-review.md` requires checking hover state but its tool grant omits `browser_hover`.

## Deliberate, leave alone

`e2e-playwright-tests` not being required (stated with reason at line 305); `CLAUDE.md` being nearly empty; version pins stated exactly once; "rerun only what the change invalidated" (governs reruns after a gate, not the first pass — no loophole); Playwright wholly owned by the verifier.

Want me to apply findings 1–9 as a `docs(workflow)` slice? Note that per the repo's own rules that means a branch, `verifier`, and `code-review` before commit — and the markdownlint + `docs_test.go` guards will police the edits.

## What to run

In formal-gate mode, run every check marked as always in `AGENTS.md`, then add
the conditional checks selected by the changed files. Do not substitute an
installed or floating tool version for the pinned command.

In formal-gate mode, if an applicable suite cannot run, report it as `NOT RUN`

  `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, absent emulators, unreachable Ollama, ports

190	// continuation lines it uses. Consuming a fixed number would leave every later
191	// line unread — and since the file list is already near the wrap width, the
192	// next entry added is the one that would create that blind spot.
193	var markdownlintInvocation = regexp.MustCompile(`markdownlint-cli@(?:[^\n]*\\\n)*[^\n]*`)
194	
195	var quotedArg = regexp.MustCompile(`"([^"]+)"`)

197	// markdownlintFiles returns the sorted set of quoted paths passed to
198	// markdownlint. Comparing sets rather than matching the raw line is what makes
199	// this insensitive to where an entry is inserted: anchoring on the first
200	// element would miss anything prepended before it.
201	func markdownlintFiles(t *testing.T, content, source string) []string {
202		t.Helper()
203	
204		invocation := markdownlintInvocation.FindString(content)
205		if invocation == "" {
206			t.Fatalf("could not locate the markdownlint invocation in %s; update this pattern if the command changed", source)
207		}
208	
209		var files []string
210		for _, m := range quotedArg.FindAllStringSubmatch(invocation, -1) {
211			files = append(files, m[1])
212		}
213		if len(files) == 0 {
214			t.Fatalf("the markdownlint invocation in %s lists no files", source)
215		}

217		sort.Strings(files)

219	}

content.text:
Both fair questions. My honest read, grounded in what's actually in those files:

**`docs_test.go` — not overkill, but aimed at the smaller problem.** It guards one specific failure class: a value duplicated in two files that drifts silently (4 version pins, the Compose line, the markdownlint list). That's real — it produces green-local/red-CI, which is the most expensive kind of failure. The header comment also shows it already got pruned once: prose assertions were removed after a guard on "must remain idempotent" kept passing when the text was flipped to "may be non-idempotent." So the overreach was already cut.

The catch: **every one of the nine defects the audit found was the other class** — AGENTS.md describing the repo, where there's no second copy to diff against. `TestListedDocsExist` only checks listed → exists, never exists → listed. That's exactly why `ROADMAP.md` and four `pkg/` packages drifted invisibly while the test stayed green. So 336 lines are watching the pins that didn't rot, and nothing is watching the tables that did.

I'd keep it and consider reversing the direction on the tables later — but that's your call, and I'm not touching it in this slice.

**The subagents are the right shape.** They contain zero commands and zero version literals (mechanically enforced by `TestRegisteredSubagentsDeferToAgentSourceOfTruth`). They're generic in *content* and specific in *role and reporting format* — which is the correct split. The specificity that earns its keep is the mode distinction: `FOCUSED: RED` vs `GATE: PASS` lets the main agent tell a TDD probe from a formal gate without reading the whole report. A single generic "reviewer" agent would lose that, and with it the context-hygiene split that step 4 exists for. Three agents for three gates is right.

Now applying the fixes, per the repo's own workflow.

content.text:
GATE: PASS

The change is documentation plus one additive line in a doc guard. Every applicable command in Verification scope ran green. Nothing tied to this change blocks progress to `code-review`.

## Commands

| Command | Status | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `go version` (pin check) | PASS | `go1.26.5` — matches `actions/setup-go`; no `GOTOOLCHAIN` prefix needed |
| `node -v` (pin check) | PASS (note) | Local default `v26.5.0`; CI pins `20`. Node-dependent check rerun under `20.20.2` — see below |
| `go vet ./...` | PASS | Clean, exit 0 |
| `go test -race -cover ./...` | PASS | Green on identical rerun; first run hit an environment link failure (below) |
| `go test -race -count=1 -v ./docs/... ./infra/... ./deploy/...` | PASS | All guard subtests pass, uncached |
| `go run .../golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run` | PASS | `0 issues.` |
| `npx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.49.1 --config .markdownlint.json "AGENTS.md" "CLAUDE.md" "README.md" "docs/**/*.md"` | PASS | No findings, on both Node 26.5.0 and Node 20.20.2 |
| `tofu fmt -check -recursive` / `tofu validate` | NOT RUN | Scoped out: `infra/` unchanged. `infra/infra_test.go` itself did run under `go test` |
| Emulator-gated contracts (`pkg/store`, `pkg/outbox`, `cmd/pet-matcher`, `cmd/notification-service`, `e2e/`) | NOT RUN | `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` and `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST` unset; no durable-state, outbox, Pub/Sub delivery, or idempotency change in this diff. Those packages reported `ok` with the contracts silently skipped |
| Playwright (`npx playwright test`) | NOT RUN | Scoped out: no HTTP service behavior, rendered page, or contract change. Compose stack not started |

## Guard tests called out in the task

All three pass uncached. `TestPinnedVersionsMatchCI` (Go toolchain, golangci-lint, markdownlint-cli, OpenTofu), `TestLocalStackCommandMatchesCI`, `TestMarkdownlintFileListMatchesCI`, `TestListedDocsExist` (now including `docs/ROADMAP.md`), and `TestRegisteredSubagentsDeferToAgentSourceOfTruth` are green, as are all `infra/` and `deploy/` subtests. The reworded sentences kept every anchored form intact.

I also spot-checked the mechanical claims the rewrite added, all of which hold: `pkg/` table matches the ten directories exactly; `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/` and `cmd/web-frontend/static/sw.js` exist; `web-frontend` publishes `8082:8082` with no `depends_on`, so "needs neither Ollama nor the other services" is correct.

## Failures

No test failure is attributable to this change.

**One environment-induced failure, green on rerun.** The first `go test -race -cover ./...` failed three packages at the link stage:

```
# github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/pkg/outbox.test
.../pkg/tool/linux_amd64/link: mapping output file failed: disk quota exceeded
FAIL github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/lostpet-service [build failed]
FAIL github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/notification-service [build failed]
FAIL github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/pkg/outbox [build failed]
```

This is not a test flake and not branch-related: it is `/tmp` tmpfs exhaustion (61G, 80% full, 13G free) while three race-instrumented test binaries linked concurrently. The identical command rerun was fully green, and those three packages relinked, ran, and cached successfully. Root filesystem has 1.5T free — only the tmpfs is pressured.

## Coverage gaps

1. **New, tied to this change: the Node 20 pin is documented but unguarded.** The diff adds ``Node — `20`, matching `actions/setup-node` in CI`` to Verification scope, and in the same diff adds a paragraph asserting that `docs/docs_test.go` compares "the version pins in their exact stated wording" against `ci.yml`. That is now true for four pins and false for the fifth: the `pins` slice in `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/docs/docs_test.go` covers only Go toolchain, golangci-lint, markdownlint-cli, and OpenTofu. The Node version can drift between AGENTS.md and `ci.yml` silently. Worth noting for whoever adds the guard: `ciStep` fails closed on ambiguity, and `ci.yml` has two `actions/setup-node` steps both named `Setup Node.js` (lines 41-44 and 94-97), so neither `actions/setup-node` nor `Setup Node.js` works as a `step` marker as-is.

2. **The `docs/ROADMAP.md` line is additive, not a guard on the table it mirrors.** `TestListedDocsExist` derives its non-glob entries from `ci.yml`'s markdownlint list and then hardcodes the `docs/` names. The new entry genuinely asserts `docs/ROADMAP.md` exists and is non-empty, but nothing ties that list to AGENTS.md's project table — the test passes whether or not the table mentions ROADMAP.md. The table-versus-test drift this line just corrected by hand can recur. Pre-existing design, non-blocking.

3. Minor accuracy read on the new paragraph: `infra/infra_test.go` and `deploy/deploy_test.go` never read `AGENTS.md` — they regex `infra/opentofu/**/main.tf`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, and `deploy/cloudrun/*.yaml`. The sentence says they "guard the OpenTofu and Cloud Run artifacts the same way," which is defensible, but the follow-on "Rewording those sentences ... can therefore fail CI" reads as if AGENTS.md prose is guarded by all three files when only `docs_test.go` reads it. The subagent no-version-literals rule listed in the same sentence is also enforced by `docs_test.go`, not by infra/deploy. Wording nit for `code-review`, not a gate failure.

4. No code coverage gap of the usual kind: this diff adds no exported functions, no error paths, and no Pub/Sub handlers.

5. Fragility worth knowing: step 6's new `docker compose up --build -d web-frontend` passes `TestLocalStackCommandMatchesCI` only because it spells the flag `-d`. That test's pattern is `docker compose up --build --detach[^\n]*` and requires every match in AGENTS.md and `ci.yml` to be byte-identical to CI's three-service line. Normalizing `-d` to `--detach` later would fail that guard with a message about the Playwright stack, which will read as unrelated.

## Worth a `gh issue create` with `agent-found`

**Environment/test debt, outside this slice:** stale verifier Go build caches are accumulating in `/tmp` — 13 directories matching `/tmp/petspotr-verifier-*-go-cache` totaling 11G, alongside a 20G `/tmp/ollama-gemma4-test` fixture. since moved on. Each one could route an agent wrong:

  work would not learn that pkg/outbox and pkg/delivery are already there.

  change would record "no UI impact" and skip the only accessibility gate.

  section. Two of its four files skip silently without an emulator, and they
  cover the redelivery idempotency rule the Code Review Rules turn on, so a

- The rerun exemption at the end named a fast-forward update, which a branch

Also documents what was never written down: that docs/docs_test.go asserts this
file's wording against ci.yml inside a required job, the GOTOOLCHAIN recovery
when the local toolchain is not 1.26.5, the Node 20 pin, and the Closes versus
Part of convention that keeps a squash merge from closing an epic mid-split.

The docs_test.go change is required by the same correction: the project table
gained ROADMAP.md, and the new GOTOOLCHAIN line is a third copy of the Go pin

gh issue create --label agent-found --title "chore(verifier): clean up stale /tmp go-cache directories" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Surfaced by the `verifier` sub-agent during the branch that became #144.

## Problem

Verifier runs leave build caches behind in `/tmp` and nothing reaps them. As of
that run there were 13 directories matching `/tmp/petspotr-verifier-*-go-cache`
totalling ~11G, alongside a ~20G `/tmp/ollama-gemma4-test` fixture. Together
they held the tmpfs at 80% (61G total, ~13G free).

## Impact

This is not theoretical — it produced a real failure. The first
`go test -race -cover ./...` of that slice failed three packages at the link
stage:

```
# github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/pkg/outbox.test
.../pkg/tool/linux_amd64/link: mapping output file failed: disk quota exceeded
FAIL github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/lostpet-service [build failed]
FAIL github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/notification-service [build failed]
FAIL github.com/scottdensmore/petspotr/pkg/outbox [build failed]
```

The identical command was green on rerun. The root filesystem has 1.5T free;
only the tmpfs is under pressure, and only when several race-instrumented test
binaries link concurrently.

The failure mode is the expensive kind: it looks like a code failure, it is
intermittent, and it invites an agent to burn a gate round debugging a package
that is fine. AGENTS.md tells the verifier to distinguish environment problems
from real failures, which worked here — but the cost lands on every run until
the caches are reaped.

## Suggested fix

Give the verifier a deterministic cache location it reuses rather than a fresh
per-run directory, or reap `petspotr-verifier-*-go-cache` older than a day.
Reusing one cache is also faster.

Branch that surfaced this: `docs/agents-md-accuracy-pass` (merged as #144).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

## Problem

`GO_INTEGRATION_OLLAMA` gates `TestScoringPipeline_LiveOllamaIntegration` in
`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go`. When the variable is unset the test calls
`t.Skip` and the package still reports `ok` — identical in behaviour to the
emulator-gated contracts.

The variable name appears in **no Markdown file in the repository**. Its sibling
`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET` is documented at `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:262`.

## Why it matters

This is the same defect class #144 fixed for the emulator contracts: a silent
skip that reads as coverage. AGENTS.md now warns that emulator-gated contracts
skip silently and enumerates the packages, but that enumeration is about
emulator host variables and does not cover this one. The CI section's "do not
claim that coverage unless a task defines and runs an explicit integration
command for it" covers the risk in prose — an agent will not falsely claim live
Ollama coverage — but there is no way to discover how to actually *run* the
test, because the variable that enables it is undocumented.

## Suggested fix

Document the variable in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` next to
`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET`, with the command that runs the test and a
note about the model it requires. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` owns integration
commands; per AGENTS.md they should not be copied into AGENTS.md itself.

Worth considering alongside #146 — if the project table gains a machine guard,
a similar guard could assert that every skip-gate environment variable in the
tree is named in some Markdown file.

That's the third time this session a gate caught a claim of mine that overstated what a guard actually does — the same defect class the original audit found in AGENTS.md, reproduced by me, in the code fixing it. Worth noting given your question about whether the subagents are too specific: a generic reviewer would likely have accepted "fails closed like `ciStep`" at face value rather than diffing the two implementations.

test(docs): guard the project table against tree drift

docs_test.go guarded one class of drift: a value duplicated verbatim in
AGENTS.md and ci.yml, where the two copies can be diffed. It never guarded
the other class, where AGENTS.md describes the tree and the tree is the only
other record of itself. TestListedDocsExist asked whether everything named
exists; nothing asked whether everything that exists is named.

That direction is where the drift actually happened. Four pkg/ packages and a
doc landed unlisted and every test here stayed green through all of it, until
an audit found them by hand in #144.

TestProjectTableMatchesTree compares the cmd/, pkg/, and docs/ rows against the
filesystem in both directions. Names are set-compared after sorting, so the
table keeps whatever order reads best — pkg/ is grouped by role, not
alphabetically — while an unlisted package and a listed-but-missing one both
fail. Duplicates are kept rather than collapsed, so a doubled name fails
against the tree instead of passing as an equal set.

projectTableRow fails closed on both counts, missing and ambiguous, because
FindStringSubmatch would bind to the first of two rows claiming the same path
and report green while watching the wrong one.

TestListedDocsExist now reads its docs names from the table instead of
restating them, removing a hand-maintained mirror of the kind this file exists
to prevent.

Two limits are deliberate and recorded where the next reader will hit them:
treeEntries does not recurse, so a nested doc is linted by the docs/**/*.md
glob without being required in the table, and the three guarded cells may carry
no inline code other than the names themselves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Follow-on to #144. That PR fixed nine stale facts in `AGENTS.md` by hand; this
one makes the largest category of them impossible to reintroduce.

## Why

`docs_test.go` guarded exactly one class of drift — a value duplicated verbatim
in `AGENTS.md` and `ci.yml`, where two copies exist and can be diffed. It never
guarded the class where `AGENTS.md` describes the tree, because there is no
second copy: the tree is the only other record of itself.

`TestListedDocsExist` asked whether everything named exists. Nothing asked
whether everything that exists is named — and that is the direction that rotted.
Four `pkg/` packages and a doc landed unlisted, and every guard in the file
stayed green through all of it until an audit found them by hand.

Four of #144's nine defects were in this class.

## What

`TestProjectTableMatchesTree` compares the `cmd/`, `pkg/`, and `docs/` rows
against the filesystem in **both directions**. Names are set-compared after
sorting, so the table keeps whatever order reads best (`pkg/` is grouped by
role, not alphabetically) while an unlisted package and a listed-but-missing one
both fail. Duplicates are kept rather than collapsed, so a doubled name fails
against the tree instead of passing as a set that happens to match.

`projectTableRow` fails closed on both counts, missing **and ambiguous** —
mirroring `ciStep`. This was caught in review: the first version used
`FindStringSubmatch`, which binds to the first of two rows claiming the same
path and reports green while watching the wrong one.

`TestListedDocsExist` now reads its docs names from the table instead of
restating them, removing a hand-maintained mirror of exactly the kind this file
exists to prevent.

## Verification

A guard that is green on its first run has proven nothing, so both the verifier
and the reviewer independently perturbed the tree and the table rather than
trusting a passing suite. Across those passes, every one of these went red:

| Perturbation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unlisted new `pkg/`, `cmd/`, or `docs/*.md` entry | red, names the entry |
| Name dropped from a row while the entry exists | red (reverse direction) |
| Row names something that does not exist | red in both tests |
| Row path renamed or cell spacing reformatted | fails closed, "no longer watching anything" |
| Duplicate row, identical **and** divergent content | fails closed, ambiguity message |
| Same name listed twice in one row | red |
| Row entries reordered | green — set comparison holds |

Removing `telemetry` from the `pkg/` row reproduces the exact drift from #144.

Gates: two `verifier` passes, both `GATE: PASS` (gofmt, `go vet`,
`go test -race -cover -count=1 ./...`, `golangci-lint@v2.12.2`, markdownlint).
Two `code-review` rounds — six non-blocking findings, all taken, then
`REVIEW: APPROVED`. `ui-review` not applicable: no rendered UI change.
OpenTofu, emulator contracts, and Playwright `NOT RUN` — `infra/` unchanged, no
service-behavior change.

## Deliberate limits

Both recorded where the next reader will hit them, not left implicit:

- `treeEntries` does not recurse, so a nested doc is linted by the
  `docs/**/*.md` glob without being required in the table. `AGENTS.md` says
  "top-level" accordingly. Fine while `docs/` stays flat.
- The three guarded cells may carry no inline code other than the names
  themselves — a parenthetical like ``(each a `main` package)`` would be
  compared against the tree and fail.

EOF
